source.title: Finite-width shift of the edge of chaos in deep neural networks

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplemental material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests initialization choices and depth on fully connected networks, with training and signal/gradient propagation measures rather than the benchmark and architecture comparisons in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports training accuracy and steps to an 85% training-accuracy threshold, not final training classification error. These results do not establish zero or near-zero training error. Cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V4 through initialization comparisons, training-accuracy threshold times and success counts, and signal/gradient propagation in plain fully connected networks. It also compares orthogonal and Gaussian tanh networks at the same mean-field variances. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right but should distinguish the sources of improvement. The authors find that critical operating-point selection and first-layer scaling account for most gains over standard rules. The finite-width correction improves training speed in Gaussian networks without a resolved final-accuracy gain, and adds no resolved accuracy or speed benefit with orthogonal weights. Deep, narrow tanh networks remain constrained by compression. The theory concerns fully connected networks at initialization.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes Crinit and tests fully connected tanh and leaky-ReLU networks on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST. Its training protocol reports test accuracy and steps to a training-accuracy threshold, rather than the claim versions' specified CIFAR classification-error outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Training outcomes vary with depth, width, activation, Gaussian versus orthogonal weights, initialization point, first-layer scaling, learning rate, and compression setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The fitted Gaussian-channel information proxy for input similarities depends on compression and the depth-to-width ratio.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization controls how accurately input similarity can be recovered from random-network representations.

record.problems: Training runs cover two small datasets, two widths, and two depths; they report test accuracy and steps/counts at an 85% training-accuracy threshold rather than final training error. Some comparisons omit diverged networks from accuracy means. The authors state the experiments test operating point and first layer more than the finite-width correction.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows omitted. Results on Fashion-MNIST and several additional initialization and leaky-ReLU settings are summarized in the excerpts and authors' conclusion but not separately rowed because the catalog versions concern CIFAR error, residual shortcuts, specific initialization comparisons, stability-limit learning rates, and batch normalization.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random labels, and the specified size and regularization conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the specified tanh-convolutional and Fixup exceptions.

Convolutional initialization, 10,000-layer training, and the full range of activation-specific initialization claims. Training experiments cover fully connected networks at depths 32 and 96, rather than arbitrary trainable depths.
Learning rates relative to the initial stability threshold, catapult recovery, edge-of-stability training and threshold-related divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance attributable to normalization, and Fixup.

missing.what: Paired confirmation of the small finite-width speed benefit: 1,000 pairs give Crinit 158.5 ± 0.4 versus mean-field 165.7 ± 0.5 steps, paired difference −7.2 ± 0.4; final test-accuracy difference is unresolved.
missing.locator: Section S8.2; Table S6, final two rows

missing.what: Width-32 boundary: at L=32 Crinit needs 254 ± 4 versus 286 ± 7 steps; at L=96 mean-field reaches the threshold in 3/100 networks and Crinit in 0/100.

Direct same-variance orthogonal control: at N=64, L=96 and weight variance 1, orthogonal initialization reaches the training threshold in 100/100 networks at 197 ± 1 steps; Gaussian LeCun reaches it in 10/100 at 690 ± 39.
First-layer controls separate forward signal scaling from relative SGD update size; giving tuned zero-bias initialization Crinit's first layer removes the resolved accuracy advantage.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is warranted for V1–V3, V5 or V6. Final near-zero training error is unnecessary for testing V4. Equality between Crinit and an already effective mean-field initialization does not itself limit V4. Fashion-MNIST and additional activation settings were explicitly declared omitted, so they are not listed again as missing; they nevertheless bear on V4. Threshold times are conditional on reaching a running, smoothed training-accuracy threshold, not full-dataset final training accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training error, corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size and early stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.

Plain versus residual shortcut comparisons, higher training error at greater depth, longer training, ImageNet/CIFAR-10, and the specified special initialization or normalization-free residual recipes.
The specific Glorot, He, and orthogonal-convolution initialization claims, convolutional networks, and training at 10,000 layers.
Training above the stability limit, loss rises and recovery, sharpness behavior, and divergence relative to the stability threshold.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual networks.
